hero.lead: A nation of 41.7 million with forest across four tenths of its land and two thirds of its power renewable, whose Government plans a C$298 billion bond programme for 2026-27.

capital.heading: A bond programme at scale, and water to treat for every home.

register.name: Budget 2026: supportive and transitional homes through Build Canada Homes
register.detail: Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada · Budget 2026 · highlighted 7 November 2026 · about 25,000 homes
register.note: With C$6.5 billion to renew and strengthen the Reaching Home Initiative and support for veteran homelessness
register.text: Budget 2026 sets out C$10 billion through Build Canada Homes for about 25,000 supportive and transitional homes across Canada, part of the Government’s plan to end homelessness within 10 years. It serves the shelter standard, the furthest from reach in Canada.

register.name: Debt Management Strategy, 2026-27, as updated in Budget 2026
register.detail: Department of Finance Canada · Budget 2026, Annex 2 · bonds C$298bn · treasury bills C$284bn · green bonds C$4bn
register.note: Up C$16 billion from the C$566 billion in the Spring Economic Update 2026, all in treasury bills; the bond programme is unchanged
register.text: Gross domestic issuance of bonds and treasury bills for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Budget 2026 raises treasury bill issuance because financial requirements have increased, and keeps the bond programme at C$298 billion, with about C$4 billion of green bonds.

register.name: Debt Management Strategy, 2027-28
register.detail: Department of Finance Canada · Budget 2026, Annex 2 · bonds C$316bn · treasury bills C$290bn · foreign currencies C$5bn
register.note: 72% refinances maturing debt; includes up to C$30 billion to fund purchases of Canada Mortgage Bonds
register.text: Total borrowings projected for 2027-28, with gross bond issuance of C$316 billion, above the C$298 billion projected for 2026-27, and about C$4 billion of green bonds. The plan includes C$66 billion of loans to enterprise Crown corporations and up to C$30 billion to fund purchases of Canada Mortgage Bonds.

register.name: Loan to Enoch Cree Nation for housing-enabling infrastructure
register.detail: Canada Infrastructure Bank · financial close announced 30 October 2026 · Indigenous Community lending · about 166 new homes
register.note: Services reserve land with roads, water and wastewater systems, utilities, site preparation and solar panels
register.text: A Canada Infrastructure Bank loan to Enoch Cree Nation to service land on its reserve for development, including roads, water and wastewater systems and utilities, preparing land for approximately 166 new residential units. It serves the shelter and water standards in a First Nation community.

register.name: Loan to NB Power for Mactaquac site development
register.detail: Canada Infrastructure Bank · financial close announced 13 October 2026 · Mactaquac Generating Station, 672 MW run-of-river
register.note: The station supplies 30 per cent of New Brunswick’s legislated renewable energy requirements
register.text: A Canada Infrastructure Bank loan to New Brunswick Power for early site development of the Mactaquac Life Achievement Project: engineering, environmental investigations, regulatory reviews and early supply activities. It serves the energy standard: the station is a large source of renewable power in New Brunswick.

register.name: Seventh green bond issuance, new 10-year green bond
register.detail: Department of Finance Canada · priced 9 October 2026 · new 10-year offering · order book over C$3.6bn
register.note: Environmentally and socially responsible investors took 44 per cent; green bonds issued since March 2022 reach C$19.5 billion
register.text: A C$2 billion Government of Canada green bond, its seventh issuance of Canadian-dollar green bonds since March 2022. The Department states that green bonds help speed up projects such as green infrastructure and nature conservation; the issue is part of the federal financing plan.

register.name: One million home retrofits
register.detail: Office of the Prime Minister · announced 8 October 2026 · heat pump rebates for up to 820,000 households · 280,000 apartment units over eight years
register.note: Rebates of up to C$10,000 for below-median-income households; apartments through CMHC mortgage loan insurance and the CIB Building Retrofits Initiative
register.text: A C$2 billion federal investment to deliver one million home retrofits: a national heat pump rebate for up to 820,000 households and retrofits of 280,000 apartment units over eight years, through CMHC (up to 250,000 units) and the Canada Infrastructure Bank (30,000 units). It serves the shelter and energy standards by cutting home energy costs.

register.name: Build Canada Homes, Social Medicine Housing Initiative, Toronto
register.detail: Build Canada Homes · announced 1 October 2026 · 80 supportive homes at the first of three sites
register.note: With the City of Toronto and the University Health Network and its Foundation; about 200 supportive homes planned across three sites
register.text: Build Canada Homes funding for the first of three sites of the Social Medicine Housing Initiative in Toronto, led with the City of Toronto and the University Health Network. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund, Northwest Territories
register.detail: Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada · announced 28 September 2026 · 14 communities · up to 2,300 homes
register.note: Under the Canada–Northwest Territories agreement of more than C$74.2 million over nine years
register.text: Federal funding for water treatment plant upgrades, water storage and distribution, wastewater and solid waste infrastructure in 14 communities of the Northwest Territories, enabling up to 2,300 housing units. It serves the water and shelter standards in northern communities.

register.name: First Nations Finance Authority debenture
register.detail: First Nations Finance Authority · announced 4 June 2026 · its largest debenture to date
register.note: Lifts the Authority’s total investment in member communities past C$5 billion, across 195 First Nation governments
register.text: Pooled borrowing in the bond market for First Nation governments, which then borrow long term at lower cost than they could alone. The Authority states that the financing supports new housing, essential infrastructure, and land and business acquisitions, serving the shelter and water standards in First Nation communities.

register.name: Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund
register.detail: Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada · Budget 2024 · up to C$6bn · Saskatchewan projects announced 13 April 2026
register.note: In Saskatchewan: C$14.2 million federal, C$11.8 million provincial and C$9.5 million municipal for Regina, Saskatoon and Moose Jaw
register.text: A federal fund of up to C$6 billion for the construction and upgrading of drinking water, wastewater and stormwater systems that enable new housing. Its Saskatchewan projects of April 2026 are to support up to 29,370 housing units, serving the water and shelter standards.

register.name: First Nations Finance Authority financing
register.detail: First Nations Finance Authority · release of 26 March 2026 · Westbank First Nation, British Columbia
register.note: Raised for First Nation community development
register.text: Capital raised by the First Nations Finance Authority, the pooled borrowing body of First Nation governments under the First Nations Fiscal Management Act, to lend to its members for community development. It serves the shelter and water standards in First Nation communities.

register.name: Sixth green bond issuance, new 10-year green bond
register.detail: Department of Finance Canada · priced 4 February 2026 · new 10-year offering
register.note: Brought green bonds issued since March 2022 to C$17.5 billion
register.text: A C$2 billion Government of Canada green bond, its sixth issuance under a green bond framework that includes certain nuclear energy expenditures. The Department cites green infrastructure and nature conservation among the projects green bonds help finance; the issue is part of the federal financing plan.

register.name: Malahat Nation water and wastewater
register.detail: Canada Infrastructure Bank · Indigenous Community Infrastructure Initiative · announced 25 June 2025 · capacity for 350 new homes
register.note: Upgrades the water facility and builds a new wastewater plant to replace failing septic beds
register.text: A Canada Infrastructure Bank loan to Malahat Nation on Vancouver Island for a new water and wastewater facility that will provide clean water and create infrastructure capacity for 350 new homes. It serves the water standard and the sanitation measure of the shelter standard in a First Nation community.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Boreal forest of spruce and birch around a calm lake, Canada

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A clear turquoise mountain lake below the Rocky Mountains, Canada

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: A large hydroelectric dam on a northern river with power lines, Canada

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.
items.alt: Golden prairie wheat fields stretching toward the Rocky Mountains, Canada

items.name: The Oil and Gas
items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2021
items.text: Oil and gas already earn; the task is to turn the rent into assets that outlast it.
items.alt: An offshore oil platform in the North Atlantic off Newfoundland, Canada

items.name: Indwell
items.text: A charity that creates supportive affordable housing communities for people seeking health, wellness and belonging, and the fastest growing developer of new supportive affordable housing in Ontario by its own account. It houses tenants in 1,435 households across southwestern Ontario, and its site lists impact loans and a Hamilton community bond among the ways to finance its homes (2026).

items.name: Second Harvest
items.text: Canada’s largest food rescue organisation, which collects surplus food from more than 11,100 food donors and redistributes it through more than 4,000 non-profit partners, with its own food rescue app. For the last year, its impact page reports 126 million pounds of food rescued and redistributed and 7.2 million people supported.

items.name: Water First
items.text: A registered Canadian charity that works with Indigenous communities on water challenges, training Indigenous adults as certified water treatment plant operators. By May 2026, 73 interns from 47 Indigenous communities had graduated from its internships, and it has worked with more than 100 Indigenous communities since 2009.

items.name: Building Up
items.text: A Toronto non-profit social enterprise and contractor that trains people facing barriers to work in the construction trades and carries out energy-efficiency retrofits for social housing and lower-income households. It receives over 4,000 applications a year, accepts about 100, and has more than 900 trained alumni (2025).

items.name: SolarShare
items.text: An Ontario non-profit co-operative, 100% owned by about 2,000 members, that finances a portfolio of 51 solar photovoltaic systems, about 15 MW, by selling SolarBonds to its members; its systems have generated C$53.8 million in revenue. Its 2026 SolarBonds, open from 16 January 2026, offer up to 4.0% fixed interest over three to seven years.
